summary: Backend regression + new `modified` field verification for RetireMentorship offline-layer iteration. All 16 pytest cases passed (16/16, 100%). Verified: (1) GET /api/wp/posts/15919 returns non-null ISO `modified` string; (2) GET /api/wp/home-feed exposes `modified` on hero and every post in `latest`; (3) search=medicare returns >=1 post (retry-once logic effective); (4) categories, home-feed shape (hero/latest/videos/trending/tip), posts?category=<id>, in-process caching, HTML entity decoding, and all 401 auth guards (bogus session, missing header on /auth/me and /user/bookmarks, bad bearer token) still intact. No regressions detected.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py wp_get() fallback branch at line ~65 has a fragile heuristic (`path.endswith(tuple(f'/{i}' for i in range(10)))`) to decide dict-vs-list default. Only reliable when post_id ends in 0-9; safer to pass an explicit `default` argument or infer from response shape. Not a regression, but brittle for /posts/{id} when id ends elsewhere (n/a for numeric ids, so no runtime impact here).

transform_post assumes p is a dict; a WP 404 for /posts/{id} returns {'code':'rest_post_invalid_id',...} which would still be transformed as if a post (id/title None). Consider a guard to return 404 to client when WP returns error dict.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reuse /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (pytest, 16 cases). BASE_URL comes from EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL env with fallback to public preview URL. WP is rate-limited (429) — tests include one 10s retry where relevant. The `modified` field must remain in transform_post output for offline-layer version tracking.
